items.text: The product catalog offers prepackaged breakfast products, such as the mini-breakfast and the luxury breakfast.
The system lets a customer assemble an individual breakfast by selecting simple products from the product catalog.
A prepackaged product is composed of simple products and/or other prepackaged products (nested product composition).
An order consists of order lines, each specifying a product (simple or prepackaged) and an amount.
Each product has a unit of measure (e.g. 100 grams) and a price per unit in Euros.
The system identifies the customer by the customer number when the customer starts placing an order.
The system validates that a customer number consists of a two-digit area code, seven digits and a one-digit checksum.
An order always belongs to exactly one customer; the system does not support collective orders of several customers.
The system authenticates the customer before an order can be placed.
During authentication the system checks that the customer is not blacklisted (e.g. due to bad payment morale) and rejects blacklisted customers.
The system lets the customer add one or several products directly to the shopping cart.
The system lets the customer search for products by desired characteristics (e.g. less than 300 calories and less than € 4), shows the matching products and lets her add them to the shopping cart.
The system lets the customer create a follow-up order by selecting one of her previous orders as a blueprint, copying its products into the shopping cart.
The system lets the customer combine direct product selection, product search and a blueprint order when assembling the shopping cart of one order.
An order references at most one blueprint order.
A previous order can be used as the blueprint for any number of new orders.
Each customer has exactly one predefined address, which the system uses automatically as the delivery address of her orders.
When an order is placed, the system assigns an order number with eight digits and a checksum and shows it to the customer.
The system shows the packing clerk each placed order so that she can assemble the ordered products into a paper bag.
The system prints a label for the order bag showing the packing clerk's name, the customer's first name, surname and address, and the order number.
The system lets the packing clerk assign a delivery clerk to the order, and the label shows the assigned delivery clerk.
The system prints the invoice of an order in two copies.
The invoice shows the label data plus each ordered product with its amount and price, and the total sum of the order.
Each printed copy of an invoice gets its own invoice number.
The system calculates the optimal delivery itinerary for a delivery clerk, covering several orders in one itinerary.
The system prints the optimal delivery itinerary together with the list of orders (bags and invoices) the delivery clerk has to deliver.
The customer confirms receipt of the delivered order; one invoice copy stays with the customer as her receipt.
The system lets the customer look up the status of her order by order number and shows whether the order is already out for delivery.
The system lets the customer cancel an order by its order number.
The system rejects the cancellation of an order that has already been assembled by the packing clerk.
A cancelled order cannot be reactivated; cancellation is final.
The system does not allow changes to a placed order; to change it, the customer cancels the order and places a new one.
The system authorises users according to their role: customer, packing clerk, delivery clerk or manager.
The system lets the customer confirm the delivery of her order by entering her password in a browser on the delivery clerk's smartphone.
The system offers a public product search that anyone can use without logging in.

items.section: Placing and Canceling an Order by Text Message
items.text: The system accepts orders sent by customers as SMS text messages to the company number.

items.section: Placing and Canceling an Order by Text Message
items.text: The system parses an SMS order message containing the customer number (C), the password (W) and one or more product codes with amounts (P).

items.section: Placing and Canceling an Order by Text Message
items.text: Each product has a unique product code.

items.section: Placing and Canceling an Order by Text Message
items.text: An SMS order may contain any number of products, limited only by the maximum length of a text message.

items.section: Placing and Canceling an Order by Text Message
items.text: The system replies to an SMS order with a text message containing the assigned order number.

items.section: Placing and Canceling an Order by Text Message
items.text: The system cancels an order when it receives an SMS cancellation message containing the order number (O).
An expected-payment record for the external payment system contains the customer number, the order number, the amount in Euros and the expected payment date.
When the packing clerk has finished assembling an order, the system sends an expected-payment record to the external payment system.

Every night the system automatically prints a business report for the manager listing all orders of the day with products, amounts, packing clerk, delivery clerk, customer, customer address and order number.
